## Description

Monte Carlo confidence intervals for free and defined parameters
in models fitted in the structural equation modeling package `lavaan`
can be generated using the `semmcci` package.
`semmcci` has three main functions, namely, `MC()`, `MCMI()`, and `MCStd()`.
The output of `lavaan` is passed as the first argument
to the `MC()` function or the `MCMI()` function to generate Monte Carlo confidence intervals.
Monte Carlo confidence intervals for the standardized estimates
can also be generated by passing the output of the `MC()` function or the `MCMI()` function
to the `MCStd()` function.
The functions `MCGeneric()`, `MCFunc()`, and `Func()` generate Monte Carlo confidence intervals
for functions of parameters when the estimates and their sampling covariance matrix are supplied.
A description of the package and code examples
are presented in Pesigan and Cheung (2024, [doi:10.3758/s13428-023-02114-4](https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-023-02114-4)).

In the Monte Carlo method,
a sampling distribution of parameter estimates $\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\ast}$ is generated
from the multivariate normal distribution
using the parameter estimates $\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$
and the corresponding sampling variance-covariance matrix
$\widehat{\mathrm{Var}} \left( \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \right)$,

$$
\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}^{\ast} \sim \mathcal{N} \left( \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}, \widehat{\mathrm{Var}} \left( \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \right) \right) .
$$

Confidence intervals for defined parameters $\boldsymbol{g} \left( \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \right)$ are generated
by obtaining percentiles corresponding to $100 \left( 1 - \alpha \right) \%$
from the generated sampling distribution,
where $\alpha$ is the significance level.

## Installation

You can install the CRAN release of `semmcci` with:

```r
install.packages("semmcci")
```

You can install the development version of `semmcci` from
[GitHub](https://github.com/jeksterslab/semmcci) with:

```r
if (!require("pak")) install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("jeksterslab/semmcci")
```

## Example

A common application of the Monte Carlo method
is to generate confidence intervals for the indirect effect.
In the simple mediation model,
variable `X` has an effect on variable `Y`,
through a mediating variable `M`.
This mediating or indirect effect
is a product of path coefficients from the fitted model.

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(package = semmcci)
library(package = lavaan)
```

### Data

```{r}
#| echo = FALSE
n <- 1000
a <- 0.50
b <- 0.50
cp <- 0.25
sigmasqem <- 1 - a^2
sigmasqey <- 1 - cp^2 - a^2 * b^2 - b^2 * (1 - a^2) - 2 * cp * a * b
em <- stats::rnorm(n = n, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(x = sigmasqem))
ey <- stats::rnorm(n = n, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(x = sigmasqey))
X <- stats::rnorm(n = n)
M <- a * X + em
Y <- cp * X + b * M + ey
df <- data.frame(X, M, Y)

# Create data set with missing values.

miss <- sample(x = seq_len(length.out = dim(x = df)[1]), size = 300)
df[miss[1:100], "X"] <- NA
df[miss[101:200], "M"] <- NA
df[miss[201:300], "Y"] <- NA
```

```{r}
summary(object = df)
```

### Model Specification

The indirect effect is defined by the product of the slopes
of paths `X` to `M` labeled as `a` and `M` to `Y` labeled as `b`.
In this example, we are interested in the confidence intervals of `indirect`
defined as the product of `a` and `b` using the `:=` operator
in the `lavaan` model syntax.

```{r}
model <- "
  Y ~ cp * X + b * M
  M ~ a * X
  X ~~ X
  indirect := a * b
  direct := cp
  total := cp + (a * b)
"
```

### Monte Carlo Confidence Intervals

We can now fit the model using the `sem()` function from `lavaan`.
We use full-information maximum likelihood to deal with missing values.

```{r}
fit <- lavaan::sem(data = df, model = model, missing = "fiml")
```

The `fit` `lavaan` object can then be passed to the `MC()` function
to generate Monte Carlo confidence intervals.

```{r}
mc <- MC(lav = fit, R = 20000L, alpha = 0.05)
mc
```

### Monte Carlo Confidence Intervals - Multiple Imputation

The `MCMI()` function can be used to handle missing values using multiple imputation.
The `MCMI()` accepts the output of
`mice::mice()`,
`Amelia::amelia()`,
or a list of multiply imputed data sets.
In this example, we impute multivariate missing data under the normal model.

```{r}
mi <- mice::mice(
  data = df,
  method = "norm",
  m = 100,
  print = FALSE,
  seed = 42
)
```

We fit the model using lavaan using the default listwise deletion.

```{r}
fit <- lavaan::sem(data = df, model = model)
```

The `fit` `lavaan` object and `mi` object can then be passed to the `MCMI()` function
to generate Monte Carlo confidence intervals.

```{r}
mcmi <- MCMI(lav = fit, mi = mi, R = 20000L, alpha = 0.05, seed = 42)
mcmi
```

### Standardized Monte Carlo Confidence Intervals

Standardized Monte Carlo Confidence intervals can be generated
by passing the result
of the `MC()` function or the `MCMI()` function to `MCStd()`.

```{r}
MCStd(mc = mc, alpha = 0.05)
```

```{r}
MCStd(mc = mcmi, alpha = 0.05)
```

## Other Features

The package provides the following functions.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `MC()` | Monte Carlo confidence intervals from a `lavaan` model |
| `MCMI()` | Monte Carlo confidence intervals from a `lavaan` model fitted to multiply imputed data |
| `MCStd()` | Monte Carlo confidence intervals for the standardized estimates |
| `MCGeneric()` | Monte Carlo confidence intervals for defined parameters of any fitted model with `coef()` and `vcov()` methods |
| `MCFunc()` | Monte Carlo confidence intervals for a function of supplied estimates and their sampling covariance matrix |
| `Func()` | Confidence intervals for a function of a supplied sampling distribution |

The `coef()`, `vcov()`, `confint()`, `summary()`, and `print()` methods
are available for the returned objects.
Examples for each function are in the package vignettes.
